title: App Remover
engine_missing: The remover engine did not answer. Check that python3 is installed, or clear Engine path in the plugin settings.
engine_timeout: The remover engine took longer than a minute and was stopped. Refresh to try again.
elevate_missing: {command} is not installed, so there is no way to ask for your password. Install it, or pick another command in the plugin settings.
launcher_outside: Launcher outside your home folder, can't be removed here
launcher_gone: Its app is gone, only the launcher is left
no_match_apps: No app matches “{query}”. All packages also searches command-line tools and fonts.
nothing_listed: Nothing to show. Refresh, or switch to All packages.
skipped_rpm: rpm and dnf are not installed here, so only Flatpak apps are listed.
skipped_flatpak: Flatpak is not installed here, so only rpm packages are listed.
ledger_empty: Select what you want to remove
dependent_heading: Also removed: {n} that need what you picked
dependent_hint: These stop working without it, so dnf takes them too.
unused_hint: Libraries and data that were only there for what you picked.
blocked_hint: Nothing was removed. Go back and pick something else.
risk_protected: This removes {names}. Your system may not start or log in afterwards.
risk_big: This removes {n} packages you picked or that need them, more than {limit} (the Big removal setting). Check the second group: those are other apps that stop working.
delete_data: Also delete the Flatpak apps' own data
delete_data_hint: Their settings and files under ~/.var/app. Off keeps them, in case you reinstall.
launchers_hint: Not from a package, so nothing is uninstalled: the launcher goes to the Trash. Its app files only go if you select them.
no_files: No app files found in your home folder
app_gone: Its app is already gone; this only clears the launcher
waiting_password_hint: Removing system packages needs your password. Enter it in the prompt that just opened.
failed_names: {names} could not be removed. The reason is in the output below.
leftovers_hint: Settings and caches with the same name as what you removed. Select the ones to move to the Trash.
no_leftovers: Nothing was left behind in your home folder.

default_view.label: Open on
default_view.description: What the panel lists when it first opens.

show_unpackaged.label: Show launchers no package owns
show_unpackaged.description: Scripts and hand-made launchers. They are listed for completeness but cannot be removed here.

protected_packages.label: Packages that need a warning
protected_packages.description: Removing any of these, even as a dependency, turns the review red and asks twice. Fedora's core system, dnf's protected packages and your running desktop are always blocked; this list only warns. Clear it to go back to the built-in one.

never_remove.label: Never remove
never_remove.description: Packages or Flatpak app ids this panel will not remove, not even as a dependency of something else.

big_transaction.label: Big removal
big_transaction.description: Warn when a removal takes more than this many packages you picked or that need them. Libraries nothing else uses are not counted.

leftover_dirs.label: Folders checked for leftovers
leftover_dirs.description: Searched one level deep after a removal. Must be inside your home folder. Empty means ~/.config, ~/.local/share, ~/.local/state and ~/.cache.

elevate_command.label: Password prompt command
elevate_command.description: Runs dnf as root. Empty means pkexec, which uses whichever polkit agent is running, Noctalia's own included. run0 works too.

flatpak_delete_data.label: Delete Flatpak app data by default
flatpak_delete_data.description: Where the review's "Also delete the Flatpak apps' own data" starts.

engine_path.label: Engine path
engine_path.description: Run this appmgr instead of the one inside the plugin. Leave empty.
